blocks.heading: What a Mismatch Costs Beyond One Person
rows: Industry employability surveys in India have repeatedly found close to half of graduates are not considered job-ready by employers, degree in hand.
A credential without a market-checked skill plan does not guarantee a job. The gap between "graduated" and "employable" is exactly the gap guidance is built to close.
Gallup's 2024 State of the Global Workplace found only 14% of employees in India describe themselves as thriving, versus 34% globally.
A person who lands in the wrong-fit role does not just take a pay cut on satisfaction - they carry it daily, for years, until they do something about it.
The ILO documents that skills mismatch depresses wages for overqualified workers, cuts firm productivity and competitiveness, and lowers the return on training investment at a national level.
This is not only a personal cost. Every mismatched hire is a training rupee, a working year, and a seat that could have gone to someone the role actually fit.
